articles.headline: Moore: Marriage deficit an economic catastrophe
articles.summary: Every study shows that the decline in marriage among young men is tied to alcoholism, violent crime, drug abuse, pornography, depression, isolation, less economic success and suicide.
articles.body: The Beatles told us: “All you need is love.” They were right, but along with love must come marriage. But marriage rates have plummeted, especially among young men. A Pulitzer Prize-worthy story by Sean Salai of The Washington Times crunches all the numbers. To say they are worrisome would be a vast understatement. — In 2025, nearly twice as many men ages 18 to 39 were unmarried as were married. — There were 30.4 million unmarried men ages 18 to 39 in 2025, up 47% from 20.7 million in 2000. — In the same period, married men in this age range dropped by 15%, from 18.1 million to 15.4 million. “Such men are more likely to be lonely, prone to deaths of despair and unhappy,” according to Brad Wilcox, a University of Virginia sociologist. — Forty-two percent of working-class men are unmarried, according to educational psychologist Donna R. Turner. In 1980, 73% of working-class men were married. I could go on and with these depressing statistics. But I believe the decline in marriage and children is a threat to the American future much more dangerous than even the national debt, climate change, cancer or foreign aggression. Family is the essential organizing unit in America. Every study shows that the decline in marriage among young men is tied to alcoholism, violent crime, drug abuse, pornography, depression, isolation, less economic success and suicide. Generation X and millennials have become choosier in finding a mate and more likely to have children alone, if they have them at all. “Women have less structural need for marriage than past generations did,” said Angelica Gianchandani, a New York University finance instructor. “Rising income and education give many women a financial independence marriage once provided, and donor sperm and fertility treatment have decoupled motherhood from a partner altogether.” Women are much less likely to be religious today than in decades past. So holy matrimony is less of a lifetime priority or moral obligation. We do know that when women raise children without a father in the home — for whatever reason — their kids, especially their sons, are less successful. I’m thrashing for explanations and solutions to this deeply troubling social trend. Obviously, we are not returning to the “Father Knows Best” norms of the 1950s or 1960s. But recovery starts with admitting we have a problem. I would suggest that President Donald Trump announce a national bipartisan commission on “Rediscovering Love, Marriage and Parenthood.” One last stat to underscore the urgency of turning around these trends: The latest Census Bureau data indicate that 47% of households were headed by married couples last year, down from 78.8% in 1949. That trend MUST be reversed to advance America’s economic prosperity and human happiness. Stephen Moore is a former Trump senior economic adviser and the cofounder of Unleash Prosperity, which advocates for education freedom for all children.

articles.headline: Anthrax – Cursum Perficio
articles.summary: First album in over a decade from American metal outfit sees them look forward rather than revel in nostalgia First album in over a decade from American metal outfit sees them look forward rather than revel in nostalgia
articles.body: It’s been ten years since the last Anthrax album, For All Kings, and the band has been working on Cursum Perficio for the last three years. With such a lengthy gestation period, you would expect something quite special from the band; a real statement of intent. It’s just possible that the intent is hiding in plain sight. The translation of the album’s title, a latin phrase, is “I finish my journey”. The album’s first two songs are the scene setting instrumental Persistence Of Memory (which alludes to the band’s fifth album Persistence Of Time) and the rumbling thrash of The Long Goodbye. Is it possible that the band is getting ready to call it a day? For those of a certain vintage, Anthrax have always been a constant in the metal world. Part of the “big four” of thrash ( Metallica , Slayer and Megadeth completing the quartet), they were always the band that seemed content to stray from the path. They dabbled with hip hop for I’m The Man and later collaborated with Public Enemy for a take on Bring The Noise and a co-headline tour. Drummer Charlie Benante , guitarist/mouthpiece Scott Ian and original Anthrax bassist Dan Lilker would explore their hardcore influences with the barnstorming offshoot project Stormtroopers Of Death . When grunge started to make its presence felt, Anthrax changed direction and tapped into that sound with their Sound Of White Noise. They were always the joker in the pack. There was the Bermuda shorts period, the ninja turtles guitars, the Stephen King obsession, and the quirky cover versions (who can forget their version of Frigging In The Rigging?). And of course there was the all important MOSH PART. With Cursum Perficio however, there’s a sense that the band is looking back over the course of their career and taking stock. The razor sharp production does admittedly bring the band into the modern day, with Benante’s drums being particularly punchy and almost mechanical in tone but the first few songs of the album have a distinct “vintage Anthrax” feel to them. The rumbling bass and riffing of The Long Goodbye instantly calls to mind the Persistence Of Time era. A chugging riff underpins a heartfelt narrative about the loss of a loved one, before a huge chorus pulls things out of the mire. The first thing that becomes apparent is that vocalist Joey Belladonna is in fine form and his return to the band has been essential. It’s For The Kids harks back to the Spreading The Disease era and even alludes to Medusa’s video in the recent promo. With themes of child endangerment and all the good thoughts and prayers do, this is the political side of Anthrax making itself known. With a crushing mosh section, a lightning guitar solo from Jon Donais and a huge performance from Belladonna, it’s a classic slice of Anthrax. The first wobble comes with Everybody’s Got A Plan, which is a perfectly serviceable slab of Anthrax, but aside from a couple of nice moments and Frank Bello’s bass, it feels a little generic. Thankfully, The Edge Of Perfection follows, and shows that Anthrax still have that desire to mix things up. Some calming atmospheric chords introduce the song, and are soon consumed by a cresting wave of Black Metal. Blastbeat drums, squalls of guitar and an almost crooned vocal instantly move Anthrax into new territory. They expertly balance it out with some classic old school riffing, naturally, but adding those Norwegian influences and those tonal shifts to their sound feels like the band looking forward rather than reveling in nostalgia. Sadly, after this experimentation, things go a little flat. Infectious, sounds pretty “stock” as Lars Ulrich would put it. It’s uninspired, and does little to encourage the raising a fistful of metal skywards. The punk thrash of NYC 93, with it’s gang vocals and breakneck pace is a little better while the title track recalls Sound Of White Noise, a time when Anthrax were more a rock band than the thrashers they started out as. At this point in the album, whether Anthrax are taking stock or not, it feels like they’re running on empty. Thankfully the thunderous riffing of T.O.M.B. gets things back on track and all of a sudden the band sound energised again as they head into Watch It Go, a song switches between all out thrash charge and considered stomp at will. Ultimately, there are some classic Anthrax moments on Cursum Perficio, but that doesn’t make it an Anthrax classic. The band’s willingness to continue experimenting with their sound suggests that, despite the overtones of finality, there’s still ground for Anthrax to cover. If this album draws a line in the sand and gets the nostalgia out of the way, the next album should be a stormer. Let’s hope we don’t have to wait another ten years to find out.

articles.headline: They're not playing our song! Wrong Korean anthem played at field hockey match at Asian Games - WRAL
articles.summary: NAGOYA, Japan (AP) — South Korean field hockey players were perplexed Friday when the national anthem of North Korea was played — instead of their own — before a men’s field hockey match against Bangladesh at the Asian Games.
articles.body: NAGOYA, Japan (AP) — South Korean field hockey players were perplexed Friday when the national anthem of North Korea was played — instead of their own — before a men’s field hockey match against Bangladesh at the Asian Games. Posted 9/18/2026, 7:28:16 AM A North Korean offical wears their national flag during a ceremony for the Asian Games at the athletes village in Nagoya, Japan, Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Dita Alangkara) NAGOYA, Japan (AP) — South Korean field hockey players were perplexed Friday when the national anthem of North Korea was played — instead of their own — before a men’s field hockey match against Bangladesh at the Asian Games. South Korean players looked on, unsure of how to respond. Many South Korean players stood at attention, some ran their hands through their hair, and some left their right hand over their heart as the music played. Other WRAL Top Stories Organizers quickly corrected the problem and played the correct anthem. South Korea won the match 5-0. The Asian Games open officially on Saturday. Some matches have been played before the official opening to accommodate a crowded schedule which features more than 11,000 athletes, more than the Summer Olympics. ___ See full AP coverage of Asian sports here Copyright 2026 by The Associated Press. articles.headline: Banana vs pomegranate: Which fruit has more iron and vitamins?
articles.summary: Bananas and pomegranates are both popular fruits, but their nutritional profiles are quite different. Bananas are best known for their potassium and vitamin B6 content, while pomegranates provide more folate,...
articles.body: Bananas and pomegranates are both popular fruits, but their nutritional profiles are quite different. Bananas are best known for their potassium and vitamin B6 content, while pomegranates provide more folate, vitamin C, fibre and beneficial plant compounds. But when it comes to iron, which fruit actually has more? The difference may be smaller than you expect. Understanding how these fruits compare can help you choose based on your specific nutritional needs rather than assuming one is healthier overall. Here’s how bananas and pomegranates stack up, nutrient by nutrient. Which fruit has more iron? If iron is the main reason you are choosing between the two, the difference is actually quite small. Per 100 grams of edible fruit, a banana contains about 0.26 mg of iron, while pomegranate arils provide roughly 0.3 mg. That gives pomegranate a slight edge, although neither fruit is considered a particularly rich source of iron. This is important because eating pomegranate or bananas alone is unlikely to make a major difference to iron intake. Foods such as legumes, meat, seafood, fortified cereals, seeds and leafy green vegetables generally provide substantially more iron. Pomegranate is sometimes promoted specifically for anaemia because of its iron content. However, the scientific evidence is more nuanced. A 2024 narrative review examined research into pomegranate juice and iron-deficiency anaemia and suggested that its bioactive compounds may potentially influence iron metabolism and absorption. The authors also stressed that more research is needed before pomegranate can be considered an established treatment for iron-deficiency anaemia. Banana has the advantage when it comes to vitamin B6 This is where the banana pulls ahead. A 100-gram serving of banana provides approximately 0.37 mg of vitamin B6, compared with around 0.08 mg in pomegranate arils. Vitamin B6 is involved in several important processes in the body, including protein metabolism and the production of neurotransmitters and haemoglobin. Bananas therefore make a useful everyday source of this vitamin, particularly when eaten as part of a varied diet. A 2023 review of banana nutrition also highlights the fruit’s contribution of vitamin B6, potassium and other micronutrients, although nutritional values can vary depending on variety and ripeness. Pomegranate offers more folate and vitamin C Pomegranate has an advantage in several other vitamins. Per 100 grams, pomegranate arils contain approximately 38 micrograms of folate, compared with about 20 micrograms in banana. Folate is particularly important for DNA synthesis and cell division. Pomegranate also contains slightly more vitamin C, with roughly 10 mg per 100 grams, compared with about 9 mg in banana. Neither fruit should be considered a major vitamin C source compared with foods such as guava, oranges, kiwi or bell peppers, but pomegranate still makes a useful contribution. A recent review published in Nutritional Review describes pomegranate as a source of vitamin C, folate and potassium, alongside a range of bioactive compounds such as punicalagin, ellagic acid and anthocyanins. The biggest difference is not actually iron The nutritional story becomes more interesting when compounds beyond basic vitamins and minerals are considered. Pomegranate is particularly rich in polyphenols, plant compounds that have been widely studied for their antioxidant and other biological activities. A 2021 systematic review published in ScienceDirect examined 86 human studies involving pomegranate juice and extracts. It found that the most promising human evidence related to blood pressure, although the researchers noted that results across studies remained inconsistent and that stronger research is needed for many of the health claims associated with pomegranate. A 2024 review published in the National Library of Medicine’s PubMed database found that pomegranate may have antidepressant- and anxiety-reducing effects, although most of the evidence so far comes from animal studies. Researchers suggested that its polyphenols may influence serotonin, estrogen receptors and PPARγ pathways involved in mood and stress responses. The review also highlighted pomegranate’s antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, while noting that more randomised, placebo-controlled human studies are needed to establish its effects. However, this does not mean that eating pomegranate prevents or treats disease on its own. Bananas are a convenient source of potassium, vitamin B6 and carbohydrates, making them useful for everyday nutrition and energy. Their natural carbohydrates can provide a quick energy boost, while potassium supports normal muscle and nerve function. Vitamin B6 also contributes to energy metabolism and normal red blood cell formation. Banana vs pomegranate: Nutrient comparison Nutrient per 100 g Per 100 g, bananas contain 0.26 mg of iron, 8.7 mg of vitamin C, 0.37 mg of vitamin B6, 20 μg of folate, 358 mg of potassium and 2.6 g of fibre. Pomegranate arils contain 0.30 mg of iron, 10.2 mg of vitamin C, 0.08 mg of vitamin B6, 38 μg of folate, 236 mg of potassium and 4 g of fibre. Values can vary with variety, growing conditions and serving size; USDA FoodData Central provides food-composition data on a 100-gram edible-portion basis. So, banana or pomegranate? For iron, pomegranate has a slight advantage, but the difference is too small to make either fruit an important iron source. For vitamin B6 and potassium, banana comes ahead. For folate, vitamin C and polyphenols, pomegranate has more to offer. The simplest approach is not to treat the two as competing fruits. Bananas can provide potassium and vitamin B6 in an inexpensive, convenient package, while pomegranate adds fibre, folate, vitamin C and a distinctive range of polyphenols. And if the concern is iron deficiency, neither fruit should replace an iron-rich diet or medical treatment. For people with confirmed iron-deficiency anaemia, identifying the cause and getting adequate iron through appropriate dietary or medical treatment is much more important than choosing between these two fruits.

raw_detail.body: Bananas and pomegranates are both popular fruits, but their nutritional profiles are quite different. Bananas are best known for their potassium and vitamin B6 content, while pomegranates provide more folate, vitamin C, fibre and beneficial plant compounds. But when it comes to iron, which fruit actually has more? The difference may be smaller than you expect. Understanding how these fruits compare can help you choose based on your specific nutritional needs rather than assuming one is healthier overall. Here’s how bananas and pomegranates stack up, nutrient by nutrient. Which fruit has more iron? If iron is the main reason you are choosing between the two, the difference is actually quite small. Per 100 grams of edible fruit, a banana contains about 0.26 mg of iron, while pomegranate arils provide roughly 0.3 mg. That gives pomegranate a slight edge, although neither fruit is considered a particularly rich source of iron. This is important because eating pomegranate or bananas alone is unlikely to make a major difference to iron intake. Foods such as legumes, meat, seafood, fortified cereals, seeds and leafy green vegetables generally provide substantially more iron. Pomegranate is sometimes promoted specifically for anaemia because of its iron content. However, the scientific evidence is more nuanced. A 2024 narrative review examined research into pomegranate juice and iron-deficiency anaemia and suggested that its bioactive compounds may potentially influence iron metabolism and absorption. The authors also stressed that more research is needed before pomegranate can be considered an established treatment for iron-deficiency anaemia. Banana has the advantage when it comes to vitamin B6 This is where the banana pulls ahead. A 100-gram serving of banana provides approximately 0.37 mg of vitamin B6, compared with around 0.08 mg in pomegranate arils. Vitamin B6 is involved in several important processes in the body, including protein metabolism and the production of neurotransmitters and haemoglobin. Bananas therefore make a useful everyday source of this vitamin, particularly when eaten as part of a varied diet. A 2023 review of banana nutrition also highlights the fruit’s contribution of vitamin B6, potassium and other micronutrients, although nutritional values can vary depending on variety and ripeness. Pomegranate offers more folate and vitamin C Pomegranate has an advantage in several other vitamins. Per 100 grams, pomegranate arils contain approximately 38 micrograms of folate, compared with about 20 micrograms in banana. Folate is particularly important for DNA synthesis and cell division. Pomegranate also contains slightly more vitamin C, with roughly 10 mg per 100 grams, compared with about 9 mg in banana. Neither fruit should be considered a major vitamin C source compared with foods such as guava, oranges, kiwi or bell peppers, but pomegranate still makes a useful contribution. A recent review published in Nutritional Review describes pomegranate as a source of vitamin C, folate and potassium, alongside a range of bioactive compounds such as punicalagin, ellagic acid and anthocyanins. Pomegranate is particularly rich in polyphenols, plant compounds that have been widely studied for their antioxidant and other biological activities. articles.headline: The Portland Thorns defense is one of its worst ever - Equalizer Soccer
articles.summary: Photo Credit: Mary Grace Grabill / Chicago Stars FC Not many teams would have been able to top Angel City’s 2024 feat of dropping 20 points from winning or drawing positions. This season’s Portland Thorns...
articles.body: Photo Credit: Mary Grace Grabill / Chicago Stars FC Not many teams would have been able to top Angel City’s 2024 feat of dropping 20 points from winning or drawing positions. This season’s Portland Thorns have done just that, and in the same amount of games. Sunday’s at-the-death equalizer from the visiting Chicago Stars brought the Thorns’ dropped points total to 23, an astounding figure. If they’d managed to hold onto even half of those, they would be Shield contenders. Instead, they are scrapping to keep their playoff position. Everyone knows why. While it may be true that the North Carolina Courage have produced a worse defensive record than the Thorns, it is also true that the Houston Dash have produced a better one. The Courage haven’t dropped so many results, either. There’s no hiding the 2026 Thorns’ ugly defensive struggles. Indeed, the club is on track for their worst defensive season in a decade. articles.headline: Prince Harry Steps Out Without Meghan Markle for First Official Outing After UK Return
articles.summary: Prince Harry made his first official UK outing as he attended the Invictus Spirit Gala Dinner & Awards. The Duke of Sussex arrived alone, without his wife, Meghan Markle. The couple relocated from their...
articles.body: Prince Harry made his first official UK outing as he attended the Invictus Spirit Gala Dinner & Awards. The Duke of Sussex arrived alone, without his wife, Meghan Markle . The couple relocated from their Montecito home on August 26 and are currently staying at a non-royal base outside London. Prince Harry's solo appearance during his latest UK visit Prince Harry made a solo appearance at the Invictus Spirit Gala Dinner & Awards at the Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich, London. For the event, he sported a black tuxedo with a bow tie and military medals near his suit pocket. He also wore his Royal Victorian Order medal beneath the bow tie. He was also asked about his thoughts on being back in the UK. He said to PEOPLE , "Good. It's good to be back on British soil." In addition, it was reported that he took selfies and photos with other guests, including two former Invictus competitors. Recently, a source told HELLO! that Meghan Markle was also spotted on a solo drive in the Cotswolds. It was reported that she was driving a large SUV and that Harry wasn't present. This was a rare sighting of Markle behind the wheel since the Sussexes returned to the UK. Both solo outings come amid the family making waves for their kids' recent school change and over their escalating tensions with Buckingham Palace over the recently released guidance letter. It's understood that Archie and Lilibet have changed schools within a few days of joining due to security concerns. Meanwhile, Buckingham Palace recently issued a letter that clarified the Sussexes' working status. The letter stated that they are private individuals and that any of their charitable work is personal, not connected to the royal family. It was reported that Markle and Harry particularly took issue with the word "private citizens," as they preferred being labeled as public figures. The post Prince Harry Steps Out Without Meghan Markle for First Official Outing After UK Return appeared first on Mandatory .

articles.headline: Tom Cruise was 'schooled' on football by Taylor Swift at NFL game - yahoo.com
articles.summary: Tom Cruise has joked that Taylor Swift "schooled" him on American football at a recent National Football League (NFL) game.On Monday, the Top Gun: Maverick actor sat next to the music superstar in a box at...
articles.body: Tom Cruise has joked that Taylor Swift "schooled" him on American football at a recent National Football League (NFL) game. On Monday, the Top Gun: Maverick actor sat next to the music superstar in a box at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri, to watch the Kansas City Chiefs play the Denver Broncos. During an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on Thursday night, host Jimmy asked Tom what it was like to sit next to Taylor. "(Taylor) was schooling me on football. For real. She was bringing the football," he smiled. "I hadn't been to a football game since pre-Covid. So, to get to hang out there and to have that moment, (it) was a lot of fun." In addition, Tom noted that it was great to see Taylor and her husband, Kansas City Chiefs player Travis Kelce. "They're a beautiful couple and magical in their own right," the 64-year-old gushed. And the Mission: Impossible star also revealed that Taylor told him Travis was "very patient" with her when they first started dating and she was learning about the NFL. "I'm sure he was," he teased. "I think anybody would be very patient... She's funny, she's got such a great sense of humour, (is) a brilliant writer, brilliant musician, director, very skilled." Elsewhere in the interview, Tom promoted his new movie, Digger. Responding to rumours that the Alejandro G. Iñárritu-directed film is actually a musical, the action man insisted it isn't. "No, but I think it's a very good idea. I think we should do Digger: The Musical," he added. Digger will open in cinemas on 2 October.

articles.headline: What happens when SpaceX Dragon retires? Boeing’s Starliner may become NASA’s primary vehicle to space: Report
articles.summary: NASA is likely to order two additional Starliner crewed missions to the station as SpaceX is looking to retire the Dragon spacecraft. NASA is reportedly mulling over awarding more missions to...
articles.body: NASA is likely to order two additional Starliner crewed missions to the station as SpaceX is looking to retire the Dragon spacecraft. NASA is reportedly mulling over awarding more missions to Boeing’s Starliner as the agency is looking for alternatives to SpaceX ’s Dragon spacecraft. Dragon has been NASA's primary source of transportation for crew and cargo to the International Space Station (ISS), but its potential retirement in a few years has prompted the agency to think about investing in other reliable partners. This artist's illustration shows the SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft docking with the International Space Station. (Representative Image Source: NASA) According to Ars Technica , NASA is likely to order two additional Starliner crewed missions to the station and help it fix the spacecraft’s problems in order to certify it for launch on a new rocket. SpaceX is reportedly looking to retire the Crew Dragon spacecraft by 2030, as the company wants to pool its resources into developing Starship for NASA’s Artemis program and future missions to Mars. CEO Elon Musk even said last month that improving Starship’s launch rate would also require winding down the Falcon 9 rocket —the primary launcher for crew and cargo missions to the space station. Boeing's Starliner spacecraft docked at the International Space Station, July 3, 2024. (Image Source: NASA) SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell believes that Boeing should step up and launch missions for NASA, hinting that Starliner may have to fill in for Dragon when it retires. “We’re not retiring it today, for sure,” Shotwell said on the All-in-One podcast and brought up Boeing, which has been entrusted with key missions by NASA in the past. “There is another provider, Boeing has been paid, I think, probably more than we have been paid to develop their human capsule. So we’re just gonna let them have some business. They should fly their capsule. The government paid a lot of money for that.” A SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft with its nosecone open approaches the ISS. (Image Source: NASA) Boeing and SpaceX were first awarded contracts for crew launch services by NASA in 2014. Under the Commercial Crew Transportation Capability contract, Boeing received $4.2 billion, whereas SpaceX received $2.6 billion. Despite receiving significantly lower funding than its competitor, SpaceX reached the finish line first by launching astronauts to the station in May 2020 under the Demo-2 mission. It marked the first time astronauts had flown to space from American soil on an American rocket since the conclusion of the Space Shuttle Program in 2011. NASA’s Boeing Crew Flight Test Commander Butch Wilmore (L) and Pilot Suni Williams walk out of the Operations and Checkout Building on June 05, 2024, in Cape Canaveral, Florida. (Image Source: Joe Raedle/Getty Images) Starliner, on the other hand, has been fraught with technical problems. Boeing has launched Starliner thrice to date, one of which was the infamous crew test flight, which, originally planned as an eight-to-14-day mission, had the astronauts stay on the space station for nine months due to several issues with the spacecraft. Launched on June 5, 2024, the test flight had former NASA astronauts Barry Wilmore and Sunita Williams on board. While Starliner was on Earth, it faced a helium leak at the launch pad, and when it reached space, the spacecraft faced thruster issues, which made docking with the space station a near-fatal task. This problem forced NASA to abandon Starliner and bring the duo home on a Dragon spacecraft, and the agency later declared the mission a ‘Type A’ failure . According to Ars, NASA may provide funding to fix Starliner’s thruster problem and certify it for a new rocket, which could be United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan or Blue Origin’s New Glenn. However, it remains to be seen how much funding NASA is willing to provide Boeing to ensure it delivers on the next mission. articles.headline: Beauty shelves to training rooms: How collagen has found a place in sport
articles.summary: Collagen, long associated with skincare and wellness products, is increasingly finding a place in elite sport, where athletes are using it as part of efforts to support joints, tendons and other connective...
articles.body: Collagen, long associated with skincare and wellness products, is increasingly finding a place in elite sport, where athletes are using it as part of efforts to support joints, tendons and other connective tissues. The shift represents a new application for an ingredient already established in the consumer health and beauty market. In high-performance sport, however, the focus is less on appearance and more on helping athletes cope with the physical demands of repeated training, competition and rehabilitation. Collagen is generally consumed as peptides or powder, particularly by athletes returning from injury and those competing in sports that place greater loads on the body. Also Read According to a report in The Indian Express, Wayne Lombard, head of athletic performance for the Indian women’s hockey team, said the science around collagen use in sport is still developing. He added that athletes use it because of its potential role in supporting joints and tissues such as ligaments, the meniscus and the labrum. Injury management creates a new sports-nutrition market Collagen is a structural protein found in connective tissues, including tendons, ligaments and cartilage. For elite athletes, maintaining these tissues can be important because training involves repeated mechanical loading and, in some sports, high-impact movements. According to The Indian Express report, Lombard said athletes use collagen to strengthen soft tissues and help keep them in a condition capable of handling repeated physical stress. He also said its use becomes particularly relevant when athletes are recovering from injuries. That puts collagen in a different segment of the sports-supplement market. Rather than being promoted primarily for muscle growth or an immediate performance boost, its use is linked to the broader objective of keeping athletes available for training and competition. Research has examined whether collagen or gelatin consumed before exercise can stimulate collagen synthesis when combined with mechanical loading. However, the evidence is still developing, and collagen should not be treated as a replacement for structured training or rehabilitation. High-performance centres bring supplementation under scrutiny The growing use of collagen also reflects the changing role of sports science in Indian high-performance programmes. At the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Vijayanagar, supplementation is part of a wider system that places emphasis on nutrition, training and rehabilitation. The centre follows a “food first” approach, encouraging athletes to meet their nutritional requirements through food wherever possible. Samuel Pullinger, head of sport science at IIS Vijayanagar, said collagen is used for joint health and pain management, with supplementation timed around specific phases of training or rehabilitation. Athletes in sports such as rowing, swimming and athletics, particularly the triple jump, are among those using collagen because of the physical loads associated with their disciplines, according to the report. The approach illustrates how sports organisations are increasingly treating supplements as part of an athlete-management programme rather than standalone products. Decisions around their use can involve sports scientists, nutritionists, coaches and medical teams. Timing becomes part of the proposition Another element attracting attention is when collagen is consumed. Pullinger said collagen has a specific window in which it can be particularly useful and suggested consuming it around 45 to 60 minutes before training or a rehabilitation session. He also recommended pairing it with vitamin C. Research has explored this timing principle, with studies suggesting that consuming gelatin or collagen before exercise can increase markers of collagen synthesis. But these studies have generally been small, meaning the findings do not establish that a particular timing protocol will improve sporting results. That distinction is important as collagen moves further into the elite-sport market. The commercial opportunity lies in a more specialised product proposition — supplements designed around training and rehabilitation — rather than presenting collagen as a shortcut to improved performance. Science still puts limits on the claims The expanding use of collagen comes despite an evidence base that is still evolving. Recent research has found potential benefits for tendon adaptation and connective-tissue health, but evidence of a direct improvement in athletic performance or muscle strength is less conclusive. The emerging consensus is that collagen may have a role alongside appropriate mechanical loading, nutrition and rehabilitation, rather than functioning as a performance enhancer on its own. Pullinger also cautioned athletes against viewing collagen as a secret ingredient that could dramatically transform sporting results. For Indian sport, therefore, collagen’s significance may lie less in its promise as a miracle supplement and more in what its growing use says about the professionalisation of athlete care. As high-performance programmes invest more in recovery, injury management and sports science, supplements such as collagen are becoming another tool in the business of keeping elite athletes training and competition-ready.

Samuel Pullinger, head of sport science at IIS Vijayanagar, said collagen is used for joint health and pain management, with supplementation timed around specific phases of training or rehabilitation. Athletes in sports such as rowing, swimming and athletics, particularly the triple jump, are among those using collagen because of the physical loads associated with their disciplines, according to the report. The approach illustrates how sports organisations are increasingly treating supplements as part of an athlete-management programme rather than standalone products. Decisions around their use can involve sports scientists, nutritionists, coaches and medical teams. Timing becomes part of the proposition Another element attracting attention is when collagen is consumed. Pullinger said collagen has a specific window in which it can be particularly useful and suggested consuming it around 45 to 60 minutes before training or a rehabilitation session. He also recommended pairing it with vitamin C. Research has explored this timing principle, with studies suggesting that consuming gelatin or collagen before exercise can increase markers of collagen synthesis. But these studies have generally been small, meaning the findings do not establish that a particular timing protocol will improve sporting results. That distinction is important as collagen moves further into the elite-sport market. The commercial opportunity lies in a more specialised product proposition — supplements designed around training and rehabilitation — rather than presenting collagen as a shortcut to improved performance. Science still puts limits on the claims The expanding use of collagen comes despite an evidence base that is still evolving. Recent research has found potential benefits for tendon adaptation and connective-tissue health, but evidence of a direct improvement in athletic performance or muscle strength is less conclusive. The emerging consensus is that collagen may have a role alongside appropriate mechanical loading, nutrition and rehabilitation, rather than functioning as a performance enhancer on its own. Pullinger also cautioned athletes against viewing collagen as a secret ingredient that could dramatically transform sporting results. For Indian sport, therefore, collagen’s significance may lie less in its promise as a miracle supplement and more in what its growing use says about the professionalisation of athlete care. As high-performance programmes invest more in recovery, injury management and sports science, supplements such as collagen are becoming another tool in the business of keeping elite athletes training and competition-ready.
